questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. In my opinion (A)/a pencil is always (B)/ more preferable than a pen. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. 

In my opinion (A)/a pencil is always (B)/ more preferable than a pen. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. C.

  • In the given sentence, 'more' is used before the adjective 'preferable' which  is incorrect as preferable is already in the comparative degree of the adjective.
  • The comparative degree is used while making a comparison between two things.
    • Eg- She is more honest than him.
  • While making a comparison, we use 'than' after the adjective.
  • but with the word " prefer & preferable "to" is used in place of than 
  • We must replace the preposition 'than' with 'to'.


Correct sentence- In my opinion, a pencil is always preferable to a pen.

questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. The climate(A)/ of Mumbai (B)/ is better than Hyderabad.(C)/ No error(D)
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. 

The climate(A)/ of Mumbai (B)/ is better than Hyderabad.(C)/ No error(D)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. C.

  • 'Better' is used which is the comparative degree of the adjective 'good'.
  • The comparative degree is used while comparing two things. 
  • In the given sentence, the climate of the two places has been compared. When one thing is compared with another thing then  we should always write 'that of' in
    case of singular comparison and 'those of' in case plural comparison after the comparative degree of the adjective in that sentence.
  • Here, 'climate' is singular so we must use 'that of'.


Correct sentence- The climate of Mumbai is better than that of Hyderabad.

questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. The best known leader(A)/ among them were(B)/ Mahatma Gandhi, Sardar Patel and Jawaharlal Nehru.(C)/ No error(D)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. A.

  • The given sentence mentions the name of three leaders.

Correct sentence- The best-known leaders among them were Mahatma Gandhi, Sardar Patel, and Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. The burglar stole all the money(A)/ in the house but surprisingly missed(B)/ the jewelleries in the locker.(C)/ No error(D)
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. 

The burglar stole all the money(A)/ in the house but surprisingly missed(B)/ the jewelleries in the locker.(C)/ No error(D)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. C.

  • 'Jewellery' is an uncountable noun and does not have any plural form.
  • The use of 'jewelleries' is grammatically incorrect. While referring to multiple instances of a plural noun, we add phrases to denote the quantity such as 'all the jewellery', 'some of my jewellery', much jewellery, etc.
  • We must replace 'jewelleries' with 'jewellery' to make the sentence correct.


Correct sentence- The burglar stole all the money in the house but surprisingly missed the jewellery in the locker.

questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. No man can become a great(A)/ artist unless he(B)/ apply himself continually to his art.(C)/ No error(D)

No man can become a great(A)/ artist unless he(B)/ apply himself continually to his art.(C)/ No error(D)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. C.

  • We need to follow subject-verb agreement rules in a sentence. If the subject is singular, we use the singular form of the verb and if the subject is plural, we use the plural form of the verb.
  • Here, the subject is 'he' which is singular pronoun so we need to use the singular form of verb i.e. applies in part C.


Correct sentence- No man can become a great artist unless he applies himself continually to his art.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into 4 parts, one of which contains an error. Select the option with the error. Scarcely had he gone(A)/ than I remembered(B)/ his name.(C)/ No error
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into 4 parts, one of which contains an error. Select the option with the error.

Scarcely had he gone(A)/ than I remembered(B)/ his name.(C)/ No error
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. B.

Explanation-

  • The conjunction 'Scarcely....when' is correlative conjunction that is used to denote two simultaneous actions in the past.
    • Eg- Scarcely had she finished eating when her parents came.
    • It's always used in pair i.e 'Scarcely....when' no other word can be used in place of 'when'
  • So, in part B we need to replace 'than' with 'when'.

​Thus, the correct option is 2 and therefore the answer.

Correct sentence- Scarcely had he gone when I remembered his name.

questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. The patient died(A)/ despite he had received(B)/ the best medical help.(C)/ No error(D)
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. 

The patient died(A)/ despite he had received(B)/ the best medical help.(C)/ No error(D)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'B'.

Key Points

  • The sentence contains an error in part B where it says "despite he had received." This is grammatically incorrect.
  • "Despite" is a preposition, and it should be followed by a noun or a gerund (ing-form verb acting as a noun).
  • Therefore, we cannot use "he had received" after "despite." Instead of using a clause after this preposition, we should use a noun phrase.
  • The correct way to phrase this would be "despite having received". 'Having received' here acts as a gerund phrase following the preposition 'despite'.
  • This way, it indicates that the action of the best medical help being received did not prevent the sad outcome.
  • This rule is universally applicable i.e., whenever you use the word 'despite', it should be followed by a noun, a noun phrase, or a gerund.
  • Correct sentence- "The patient died despite having received the best medical help."

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

questions.solution:

  • In the given sentence, the speaker is talking about a specific man in the corner.
  • The most appropriate word should be 'the'.

Correct sentence- The man standing in that corner is a police man in plain clothes.

questions.question: Directions: In this section, each of the following sentences has a blank space and each sentence is followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill the blank space. Eight cylinder engines are _______ that use great amount of petrol.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: In this section, each of the following sentences has a blank space and each sentence is followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill the blank space.

Eight cylinder engines are _______ that use great amount of petrol.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. devices.

Let us look at the meanings of the given words-

  • Conveyances means the action or process of transporting or carrying someone or something from one place to another.
  • Devices means a thing made or adapted for a particular purpose, especially a piece of mechanical or electronic equipment.
  • Instruments mean a tool or implement, especially one for precision work.
  • Apparatus means the technical equipment or machinery needed for a particular activity or purpose.


Clearly, eight-cylinder engines can be described as 'mechanical equipment'.

Correct sentence- Eight cylinder engines are devices that use great amount of petrol.

The most appropriate word is 'procrastinate' as the sentence describes how he would be late for submissions because he used to delay everything.

Correct sentence- He would always be late with submissions because he would procrastinate whatever he was supposed to do.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word. Evince

Evince

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word. Pernicious

Pernicious

   Explanation

  • Injurious means causing or likely to cause damage or harm.

​Here we find that both Pernicious and Injurious express similar meanings.

Therefore Option 4 Injurious is the correct answer.

Let's look at the meaning of other words:

  • Filthy means disgustingly dirty.
  • Foul means offensive to the senses, especially through having a disgusting smell or taste or being dirty.
  • Continuous means forming an unbroken whole; without interruption.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word. Eulogy
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word. 

Eulogy
questions.solution:
The answer is Option 3 i.e Praise

   Explanation

Let's look at the meaning of the given word and the option:

  • Eulogy: A speech or piece of writing that praises someone or something highly, especially a tribute to someone who has just died. 
  • Praise means express warm approval or admiration of.

​Here we find that both Eulogy and Praise express similar meanings.

Therefore Option 3 Praise is the correct answer.

Let's look at the meaning of other words:

  • Harmony: The state of being in agreement or concord.

  • Option 3) Allowed us to enjoy the works of great writers.   • Option 4) Given translation its rightful place.
